name: Familial Intrahepatic Cholestasis

criteria.description: Chronic cholestasis presenting in infancy or early childhood with pruritus and jaundice
Elevated serum bile acids with normal or low gamma-glutamyl transferase (GGT) levels
Identification of pathogenic mutations in genes associated with PFIC (e.g., ATP8B1, ABCB11, ABCB4)
Histopathological evidence of intrahepatic cholestasis with absence of bile duct obstruction
Positive family history of cholestatic liver disease or consanguinity

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of chronic cholestasis with pruritus and jaundice in infancy or early childhood, low/normal GGT cholestasis biochemical profile, and confirmation by genetic testing
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Liver biopsy and family history support diagnosis but are not mandatory if genetic testing confirms pathogenic variants.

pathognomonic.notes: Intense itching often refractory to standard treatments
searchTerms: itching due to liver bile problems

pathognomonic.notes: Yellow discoloration of skin and sclera due to bile retention

pathognomonic.symptomName: Low or normal serum gamma-glutamyl transferase (GGT) levels despite cholestasis
pathognomonic.notes: Characteristic biochemical hallmark distinguishing PFIC from other cholestatic diseases
searchTerms: low or normal GGT despite cholestasis
normal liver enzyme with bile flow problems

common.notes: Poor weight gain and growth delay in affected children
Fatty, foul-smelling stools secondary to impaired bile flow
searchTerms: fatty stools from poor fat absorption

common.symptomName: Fat-soluble vitamin deficiencies (A, D, E, K)
common.notes: Manifesting as bleeding tendency, bone disease, or visual disturbances
searchTerms: lack of vitamins A, D, E, K

common.notes: Enlarged spleen due to portal hypertension in advanced disease

occasional.notes: Cholesterol deposits in skin due to impaired bile acid secretion
Non-specific symptoms related to chronic illness

occasional.symptomName: Prurigo nodularis secondary to chronic scratching
occasional.notes: Skin nodules caused by persistent itching
searchTerms: skin bumps caused by chronic scratching

occasional.notes: Elevated liver enzymes ALT and AST
searchTerms: liver cell damage from bile buildup

rare.symptomName: Progression to cirrhosis and liver failure
rare.notes: End-stage liver disease in untreated or severe cases
Rare malignant transformation in chronic cholestasis

rare.symptomName: Neurological complications due to vitamin E deficiency
searchTerms: neurological problems from vitamin E lack
nerve issues due to vitamin E deficiency

rare.symptomName: Coagulopathy due to vitamin K deficiency
searchTerms: bleeding problems from vitamin K lack
blood clotting issues due to vitamin deficiency
coagulopathy linked to vitamin K shortage

imaging: Ultrasound showing hepatomegaly without biliary obstruction
Liver elastography indicating fibrosis or cirrhosis
genetic: Pathogenic mutations in ATP8B1 (PFIC1), ABCB11 (PFIC2), ABCB4 (PFIC3) genes
other: Liver biopsy showing canalicular cholestasis and absence of bile duct obstruction

distinguishingFeatures: Absence of pathogenic PFIC gene mutations
Early onset with progressive biliary obstruction
Characteristic facial features and cardiac anomalies

redFlags: Progressive jaundice with intense pruritus in infancy
Failure to thrive despite nutritional support
Development of coagulopathy or bleeding tendency
references: Strautnieks SS, Thompson RJ, et al. The molecular basis of progressive familial intrahepatic cholestasis. Gut. 2008.
Bull LN, Thompson RJ. Progressive familial intrahepatic cholestasis. Clin Liver Dis. 2018.
